objective: Reduce model-context overhead for large MCP-like tool registries through deterministic capability/trust filtering, byte budgets, generation fencing, receipt integrity, and bounded result projection without granting model output or provider metadata authority.

research.conclusion: Current inference runtimes emphasize prefix caching, continuous batching, structured outputs, tool/reasoning parsers, multimodal execution, and provider/hardware adapters.
research.implementation_impact: FAISAL should expose runtime observations and policies through provider-neutral control-plane contracts rather than embed a runtime or model provider in privileged code.

research.conclusion: Speculative decoding supports multiple methods and documents workload-dependent gains, compatibility constraints, and lossless-validation boundaries.
research.implementation_impact: Any future latency optimizer must be measured per workload and bounded by explicit compatibility and rollback policy.

research.conclusion: SGLang emphasizes RadixAttention/prefix caching, low-latency scheduling, multimodal models, and broad accelerator support.
research.implementation_impact: FAISAL can model cache locality and accelerator observations as untrusted inputs for adaptive control, not as privileged authority.

research.conclusion: MCP defines resources, prompts, tools, capability negotiation, cancellation, progress, asynchronous tasks, and explicit consent/tool-safety guidance.
research.implementation_impact: FAISAL needs progressive capability-scoped admission and deterministic tool/result governance at the control-plane boundary.

research.conclusion: Computer-use integrations require isolated browser/VM environments, explicit action boundaries, untrusted page content, and human control for high-impact actions.
research.implementation_impact: The tool-context layer must not authorize browser or computer actions; it only bounds context and preserves provenance for a separately authorized sandbox.

research.conclusion: Progressive tool discovery and code execution can reduce context transfer, while generated execution requires sandboxing, resource limits, and monitoring.
research.implementation_impact: FAISAL implements deterministic admission and metadata-only result projection, leaving code execution to an isolated userspace sandbox.

features: deterministic registry-order admission and stable selected IDs
registry generation fencing for stale requests and receipts
SHA-256 definition, admission, original-result, projected-result, and receipt digests
tamper rejection for receipt counters and digest fields
metadata-only bounded result projection without returning payload contents
model-proposal and verified-input flags retained as non-authoritative metadata
fail-closed malformed request and oversized-result handling

validation.selftest: FTC_TOOL_CONTEXT_SELFTEST_OK cases=18 selected=1 skipped=4 projected_definition=81 projected_result=400 generation=2

benchmark.interpretation: The progressive planner admitted 25.8% of the full fixture definition bytes, a 74.2% reduction. The baseline is a local full-manifest byte scan, not a model-inference or end-to-end latency comparison; the planner adds digest and policy work by design.

live_model_catalog.interpretation: The live catalog was researched for adapter/routing design only; no model ID or provider metadata is treated as authorization or hard-coded into privileged code.

qualification_limits: This is a bounded userspace/control-plane contract and does not implement an MCP client, browser driver, code-execution sandbox, model inference engine, or physical accelerator path.
The 74.2% context-byte reduction is measured on the deterministic eight-tool fixture and does not claim proportional token, latency, cost, or quality improvement for any provider or model.
The benchmark’s full-manifest baseline is intentionally simpler than the integrity-checked planner and must not be presented as an apples-to-apples latency superiority result.
No live external tool invocation, paid model call, browser session, robotics device, GPU/NPU, or production cluster was used; no such qualification is claimed.
The registry and receipts remain userspace/reference contracts until separately integrated with a production service, capability broker, audit journal, and independent security review.
